summary: Palmo Kyi works in the field of Tibetology. She studied under supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012) and teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University from around 1972 to 1976.

Panahaduwe Yasassi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Professor in Buddhist Civilization at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura in 2020 and as Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai, his career included teaching law at Government Law College (~1917–1923) and serving as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

Pankaj Tandon works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Mentored by Tom Mallon-McCorgray, he earned degrees from St. Stephen's College (B.A. 1971), Delhi School of Economics (M.A. 1973), and Harvard University (Ph.D. 1979), becoming Associate Professor at Boston University in 1978.

Paolo Daffinà (d. 2009) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, history, and archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at Sapienza University of Rome in 1953 under Giuseppe Tucci, Luciano Petech, and Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, later serving there as Director (1973–1982).

Paolo Emilio Pavolini (1864–1942) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Pisa and Humboldt University of Berlin under Emilio Teza, Albrecht Weber, and Richard Pischel, later serving as Professore ordinario at the University of Florence (1895–1935).

Paolo Visigalli is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Padua, Sapienza University of Rome, and the University of Cambridge. He has held posts at NYU Shanghai and Shanghai Normal University (attested 2025).

Paramahansa Yogananda (1893–1952) was active in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1910–1912), the Senate of Serampore College (~1913–1915), and the University of Calcutta (~1910–1915).

Paramita Paul works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Leiden University in 2009 and has held posts as Lecturer at Amsterdam University College and Chief Editor at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and Sylvain Lévi (~1921–1923), later serving as Director of the Mithila Institute (~1954–1958) and General Editor at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1961–1972).

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (2013–2022) and held postdoctoral posts at the University of Tokyo (2022–2023) and Ghent University (2023).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1991–1993) and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), he became a Professor at Harvard University around 2005.

Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, history, and archaeology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1986–1991) and served as a Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2006–2026).

Pascale Haag (b. 1965) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and Marie-Claire Gay, earning doctorates from Sorbonne Nouvelle (2002) and Paris Nanterre (2018), and became an Associate Professor at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2003.

Pascale Hugon specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed a Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post as Professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Bristol, the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012), and the Max Planck Society as a Senior Research Fellow in 2016.

Patricia Berger specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman; her posts include Curator at the Asian Art Museum and Professor Emerita at UC Berkeley (1996).
